reading.body:
Louisiana's tracked data center footprint is thin: four facilities, concentrated in Baton Rouge and Shreveport, with only 3 MW of confirmed capacity recorded across the entire state.

DartPoints operates three of the four facilities, and the only capacity figure in the data, 3 MW, belongs to a single DartPoints site in Baton Rouge. The remaining three facilities carry no megawatt figures, so the 3 MW total reflects what is reported, not necessarily what exists. The Center for Computation and Technology in East Baton Rouge Parish is the sole non-commercial entry, suggesting a research or academic function rather than commercial colocation.

At 3 MW of confirmed capacity, Louisiana sits far below the scale at which data center infrastructure meaningfully supports large AI workloads. Serious model training typically requires dedicated power measured in tens or hundreds of megawatts at a single site. What the data does not cover includes any planned expansions, utility interconnection queues, or facilities that operators have not disclosed publicly, all of which would bear directly on the state's realistic ceiling for AI compute.
